subject: Re: Cloudfolio bakeoff - proposed short-term bridge & next steps
messages:
From: Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@cloudfolio.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cloudfolio.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Bakeoff latency profile — urgent follow-up

Hey Rishi —

Thanks again for getting the team involved for the Cloudfolio bakeoff last week. We ran the full 72-hour window against our test harness and surfaced a couple of items that are worrying for our infra team:

- Intermittent 95th/99th p99 latency spikes during short bursts (peaked at ~1.8s on some runs, our target is <700ms for 95th).
- Higher token cost in the 8k window than the numbers you'd shown in the initial deck (we observed ~22% higher tokens/second).

We have a hard runway to finalize hosting decisions by the end of this month. Our CTO is flagging the latency variance as a material risk; they're pushing to give the upcoming evaluation to a competitor that can commit to latency SLOs and a migration window.

Can we get an explanation of what caused the spikes and a concrete mitigation path? If Redwood can offer a short-term capacity and pricing bridge while you investigate and run a repro, that would help keep us from switching.

I've attached the raw logs and the harness results (cloudfolio-bakeoff-raw.csv). Happy to hop on a call if that helps.

—Ethan
Ethan Wu
VP Engineering, Cloudfolio
ethan.wu@cloudfolio.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@cloudfolio.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cloudfolio.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bakeoff latency profile — urgent follow-up

Ethan —

Really appreciate the detailed logs and the quick flag. First: sorry for the disruption — this is taken seriously. I pulled Ben (solutions) and Marissa (CS) onto this thread so we can move fast. Quick notes and next steps below:

What we saw (initial read):
- The p99 spikes line up with multiple short-burst runs where the KV cache warmed unpredictably and we hit a fallback fast-path with slightly higher latency under the current kernel selection. That explains the intermittent nature.
- Token accounting difference is likely due to prefix handling in your harness and how your test truncated / padded sequences; we'll repro with your exact harness to be sure.

Proposed immediate actions (to avoid customer churn):
1) Dedicated short-term capacity: we can provision a reserved shard for Cloudfolio for 90 days (3-week ramp then stable) at an uplifted but capped rate — see attached draft (redwood-bridge-term-draft.pdf). This gives you isolation and guaranteed throughput while we stabilize.
2) Technical repro run: Ben will run a tuned repro against your harness (Ben — can you confirm availability next Tue/Wed?).
3) Canary & rollback plan: Marissa will propose a canary rollout plan so Cloudfolio can validate in production with a safety net.

If Cloudfolio is willing to sign the bridge by next Tue, we'll start the reserved shard and prioritize root-cause work. Happy to jump on a call with your CTO and infra leads.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@cloudfolio.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bakeoff latency profile — urgent follow-up

Ethan / Team —

Thanks for the logs, I ran a quick pass this morning and captured two reproducible signals:
- Kernel fallback on 4-token I/O bursts when KV cache TTLs were below expected thresholds. That produces 200–400ms variance per request in the worst path.
- A batching artifact in your harness: some of the request bursts were batched into a larger micro-batch due to client-side aggregation. That inflated per-token cost and increased tail latency on certain runs.

What I need from you to run a full repro:
1) exact harness run command and the harness version (you sent results.csv but not the run manifest)
2) a small sample harness config that reproduces the burst pattern (5–15s burst windows)

Proposed mitigation (short):
- We can pin kernel selection and raise KV cache TTLs on the reserved shard to reduce fallback events.
- We'll add a micro-batching cap in the request path for your reserved shard so client-side aggregation doesn't push large micro-batches through.

I can run the repro Tue/Wed (Oct 20–21). Rishi — if we get a signed bridge by end of Tue, I’ll prioritize infra time for the repro.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Rishi / Ben —

Appreciate the swift follow-up. We're comfortable running the repro — attaching the harness manifest and a small config (benchmark-repro-notes.txt).

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood commit to the reserved-shard start date within 48 hours of signature? We need the uplift capacity to de-risk the run.
2) Can we get a short-term SLA addendum for p95/p99 during the 90-day bridge window (we don't expect long-term SLA changes, just a guarantee for the experiment window)?

We'll aim to have procurement review the draft bridge and come back with minimal redlines by EOD Mon (Oct 25).

—Priya

Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge signed pending procurement — next steps and timelines

Priya / Ethan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Per your note: we matched the repro run today (Ben's tweaks reduced the worst-path variance to ~110–130ms). Good signal.

Commercials & next steps:
- We updated the bridge draft with a 48-hour start commitment and a 90-day reserved shard at capped uplift pricing. The DocuSign envelope is live: https://docusign.net/embeddedSigning/XXXX-bridge-offer
- The bridge includes a short-term SLA addendum for p95/p99 during the 90-day window (remediations and credits tied to measured SLOs).
- Ben & team will run the full 72-hour repro on the reserved shard starting Tue (Oct 26).
- Marissa will run a canary plan with a small rollout group and weekly checkpoints.

If procurement returns the signed agreement by EOD Wed (Oct 27) we'll start provisioning immediately. I attached the final draft and the quick reproducibility notes.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Cloudfolio stable on Redwood.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
